section_1.title: Short title, commencement and application
section_1.description: This is the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the Indian Penal Code. It applies to every person for offences committed in India, and to certain offences committed outside India, such as by Indian citizens or on Indian ships and aircraft.
key_points: Short title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
In force from 1 July 2024
Applies to offences committed within India
Extends to offences abroad by citizens and on Indian ships or aircraft

section_2.title: Definitions
section_2.description: Defines the key words and phrases used throughout the Sanhita, so that every later section is read with the same meaning.
key_points: Defines terms like child, court, document, gender, injury, public servant and woman
Child means a person below eighteen years of age

section_3.title: General explanations
section_3.description: Lays down general rules for interpreting the Sanhita. Most importantly, section 3(5) says that when several persons do an act together in furtherance of their common intention, each of them is liable as if he did the act alone.
key_points: Section 3(5) continues the old IPC 34 common-intention rule
Expressions explained here apply throughout the Sanhita

section_4.title: Punishments
section_4.description: Lists the punishments a court may impose: death, imprisonment for life, rigorous or simple imprisonment, forfeiture of property, fine, and community service.
key_points: Six kinds of punishment
Community service is a new addition under the BNS
Imprisonment may be rigorous (with hard labour) or simple

section_5.title: Commutation of sentence
section_5.description: Allows the appropriate Government to commute a death sentence to any other punishment provided by the Sanhita, without the consent of the offender.
key_points: A Government power, not a right of the convict
Applies to sentences of death

section_6.title: Fractions of terms of punishment
section_6.description: Explains how fractions of terms of punishment are calculated. For this purpose, imprisonment for life is treated as imprisonment for twenty years.
key_points: Life imprisonment counts as twenty years when working out fractions

section_7.title: Sentence may be (in certain cases of imprisonment) wholly or partly rigorous or simple
section_7.description: Where a section allows imprisonment that may be rigorous or simple, the court may order it to be wholly rigorous, wholly simple, or partly rigorous and partly simple.

section_8.title: Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc.
section_8.description: Where no fine amount is specified, the fine is unlimited but must not be excessive. It also sets the rules for imprisonment in default of payment of fine.
key_points: Fine is unlimited unless the section fixes an amount
Imprisonment in default of fine has graded limits

section_9.title: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences
section_9.description: Where an offence is made up of parts, each of which is itself an offence, the offender is punished for only one of them, unless the law expressly says otherwise.

section_10.title: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which
section_10.description: Where the judgment is doubtful as to which of several offences was committed, the offender is punished for the offence carrying the lowest punishment.

section_11.title: Solitary confinement
section_11.description: Permits courts to order solitary confinement as part of a sentence of rigorous imprisonment, subject to strict limits.
key_points: Only for offences punishable with rigorous imprisonment

section_12.title: Limit of solitary confinement
section_12.description: Caps solitary confinement: no more than three months in total, ordered in stretches of at most fourteen days with intervals in between.
key_points: Total cap of three months
Fourteen-day stretches with breaks between them

section_13.title: Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction
section_13.description: Prescribes enhanced punishment for a person previously convicted of an offence punishable with three or more years of imprisonment who commits another such offence.
key_points: Targets repeat offenders
Higher sentence on reconviction

section_14.title: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law
section_14.description: Nothing is an offence when done by a person who is bound by law to do it, or who in good faith believes, by mistake of fact, that he is bound by law to do it.
key_points: Covers mistake of fact, not mistake of law

section_15.title: Act of Judge when acting judicially
section_15.description: Protects a Judge acting judicially in the exercise of a power which he in good faith believes himself to have, even if he acts in excess of it.

section_16.title: Act done pursuant to judgment or order of Court
section_16.description: Acts done under a court's judgment or order, while it remains in force, are not offences, even if the court lacked jurisdiction, provided they were done in good faith believing it had jurisdiction.

section_17.title: Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself justified, by law
section_17.description: Nothing is an offence when done by a person who is justified by law, or who in good faith believes, by mistake of fact, that he is justified by law.

section_18.title: Accident in doing a lawful act
section_18.description: An accident occurring while doing a lawful act, in a lawful manner, with proper care and caution, is not an offence.
key_points: Requires a lawful act done lawfully and carefully

section_19.title: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm
section_19.description: An act likely to cause harm, done without criminal intent and in good faith in order to prevent or avoid greater harm to person or property, is not an offence.
key_points: The lesser-evil principle
Must be done without criminal intent

section_20.title: Act of a child under seven years of age
section_20.description: Nothing done by a child under seven years of age is an offence.
key_points: Complete exemption below the age of seven

section_21.title: Act of a child above seven and under twelve years of age of immature understanding
section_21.description: A child above seven and under twelve years of age who has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of the act is exempt from criminal liability.
key_points: Depends on the child's maturity, judged case by case

section_22.title: Act of a person of unsound mind
section_22.description: Nothing is an offence done by a person who, because of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that it is wrong or contrary to law.
key_points: The legal insanity defence
Covers inability to know the act's nature, wrongness or illegality

section_23.title: Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will
section_23.description: Acts done by a person who is incapable of judgment because of intoxication administered to him without his knowledge or against his will are not offences.
key_points: Protects only involuntary intoxication
The drink or drug must have been given without consent

section_24.title: Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated
section_24.description: Where an offence requires a particular intent or knowledge, a person who was voluntarily intoxicated is treated as if he had that intent or knowledge, unless the intoxication was involuntary.
key_points: Voluntary drunkenness is no excuse for intentional offences

section_25.title: Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent
section_25.description: An act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done with the free consent of a person above eighteen years who accepts the risk of harm, is not an offence.
key_points: Consent must be free and by an adult
Never covers acts intended to kill or maim

section_26.title: Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit
section_26.description: An act done in good faith for a person's benefit, with that person's consent, is protected even if it causes harm, provided it was not intended to cause death.
key_points: Good faith plus consent
Commonly relied on in medical situations

section_27.title: Act done in good faith for benefit of child or person of unsound mind, by, or by consent of guardian
section_27.description: A guardian's consent, express or implied, protects acts done in good faith for the benefit of a child under twelve or a person of unsound mind, except acts intended to cause death or grievous hurt and certain other excluded acts.
key_points: Guardian can consent for young children and persons of unsound mind
Death, grievous hurt and abetment of offences are never covered

section_28.title: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception
section_28.description: Consent is not valid if given under fear of injury or under a misconception of fact, or if given by a person of unsound mind or a child under twelve.
key_points: Fear or misconception vitiates consent
Children under twelve cannot give valid consent

section_29.title: Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm caused
section_29.description: Consent does not protect acts which are offences independently of any harm they cause, so the consent exceptions in sections 25 to 27 do not apply to such acts.

section_30.title: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent
section_30.description: An act done in good faith for a person's benefit without their consent is protected when it was impossible to obtain consent in time, as in an emergency.
key_points: Covers emergencies where consent cannot be obtained
Must still be done in good faith

section_31.title: Communication made in good faith
section_31.description: A communication made in good faith for a person's benefit is protected even if it causes harm to that person.

section_32.title: Act to which a person is compelled by threats
section_32.description: An act done under compulsion of threats that cause a reasonable fear of instant death is excused, except murder and offences against the State punishable with death.
key_points: Threat must cause fear of instant death
Never a defence to murder or waging war

section_33.title: Act causing slight harm
section_33.description: Trifling acts that cause only slight harm, which no person of ordinary sense and temper would complain of, are not offences.

section_34.title: Things done in private defence
section_34.description: Nothing done in the exercise of the right of private defence is an offence.
key_points: Private defence is a complete justification

section_35.title: Right of private defence of body and of property
section_35.description: Every person has a right to defend his own body and the body of any other person, and his own or another's property, against the offences listed in the following sections.
key_points: Covers defence of self, others, and property
The foundation of all private-defence claims

section_36.title: Right of private defence against act of a person of unsound mind, etc.
section_36.description: The right of private defence applies even against the act of a person of unsound mind, a child, or an intoxicated person, just as it would against a sane adult.

section_37.title: Acts against which there is no right of private defence
section_37.description: There is no right of private defence against an act done by a public servant in good faith in the execution of his duty, or at his direction, and the right never extends to causing more harm than necessary.
key_points: No defence against lawful acts of public servants
Force used must not exceed what is necessary

section_38.title: When right of private defence of body extends to causing death
section_38.description: Causing death in private defence of the body is justified where the assault reasonably causes fear of death or grievous hurt, or is an attempt to commit rape, gratify unnatural lust, kidnap, abduct, wrongfully confine, or throw acid.
key_points: Lists the grave assaults justifying lethal force
Based on reasonable apprehension of danger

section_39.title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
section_39.description: In private defence of the body against assaults less grave than those in section 38, any harm other than death may be caused.

section_40.title: Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of body
section_40.description: The right of private defence of the body begins as soon as there is a reasonable apprehension of danger and continues as long as that apprehension lasts.

section_41.title: When right of private defence of property extends to causing death
section_41.description: Causing death in private defence of property is justified against robbery, house-breaking by night, mischief by fire or explosive to a dwelling, and theft, mischief or house-trespass that reasonably causes fear of death or grievous hurt.
key_points: Lethal force only for the gravest property offences

section_42.title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
section_42.description: In private defence of property against offences less grave than those in section 41, any harm other than death may be caused.

section_43.title: Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of property
section_43.description: The right of private defence of property begins when there is a reasonable apprehension of danger to the property and continues until the danger passes or public authorities can intervene.

section_44.title: Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person
section_44.description: Where defending against a deadly assault creates a risk of harm to an innocent person, the defender may still exercise the right of private defence, taking that risk in good faith.
key_points: Good-faith risk to bystanders is excused

chapter_4.title: Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt

section_45.title: Abetment of a thing
section_45.description: Defines abetment of a thing: instigating any person to do it, engaging with others in a conspiracy to do it, or intentionally aiding its doing.
key_points: Three modes: instigation, conspiracy, and intentional aiding
Covers abetment whether or not the act is actually committed

section_46.title: Abettor
section_46.description: Defines an abettor as a person who abets the commission of an offence, or the commission of an act which would be an offence if committed by a person capable of committing it.

section_47.title: Abetment in India of offences outside India
section_47.description: A person abets an offence punishable under the Sanhita even if the abetment takes place in India while the act itself is committed outside India.

section_48.title: Abetment outside India for offence in India
section_48.description: A person outside India who abets the commission of an offence committed in India is punishable as an abettor.

section_49.title: Punishment of abetment if act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment
section_49.description: Punishes abetment with the same punishment as the abetted offence, where the abetted act is committed in consequence and no separate punishment for the abetment is provided.
key_points: Abettor faces the same sentence as the main offender

section_50.title: Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of abettor
section_50.description: Where the person abetted does the act with a different intention from the abettor's, the abettor is punished according to his own intention, as if he had abetted it with that intention.

section_51.title: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done
section_51.description: Makes the abettor liable when the person abetted does a different act from the one abetted, if that act was a probable consequence of the abetment.
key_points: Liability extends to probable consequences

section_52.title: Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done
section_52.description: Where the abettor is liable both for the abetment and for the act actually done, he may be punished cumulatively, with a separate punishment for each.

section_53.title: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by act abetted different from that intended by abettor
section_53.description: Makes the abettor liable where the effect caused by the abetted act differs from what he intended, if he knew that the different effect was likely to be caused.

section_54.title: Abettor present when offence is committed
section_54.description: An abettor who is present when the offence is committed is deemed to have committed the offence himself and is punished accordingly.
key_points: Presence at the scene equals commission

section_55.title: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
section_55.description: Punishes abetment of an offence carrying death or life imprisonment: up to seven years plus fine if the offence is not committed, and up to fourteen years plus fine if hurt is caused.
key_points: Higher punishment when the abetment leads to hurt

section_56.title: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment
section_56.description: Punishes abetment of an offence carrying imprisonment, where the offence is not committed in consequence: up to one-fourth of the longest term provided for that offence.

section_57.title: Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons
section_57.description: Punishes abetting the commission of an offence by the public generally, or by more than ten persons: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_58.title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
section_58.description: Punishes concealing a design to commit an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment: up to seven years plus fine if the offence is committed, and up to three years plus fine if it is not.

section_59.title: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent
section_59.description: Punishes a public servant who, intending to facilitate an offence, conceals a design to commit it when it was his duty to prevent it, with graded punishment reaching up to ten years for the gravest offences.
key_points: Applies only to public servants under a duty to prevent the offence

section_60.title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
section_60.description: Punishes concealing a design to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment: up to one-fourth of the longest term for that offence, or fine, or both.

section_61.title: Criminal conspiracy
section_61.description: Defines criminal conspiracy as an agreement between two or more persons to do an illegal act, or a legal act by illegal means. The agreement itself is the offence; no further overt act is required.
key_points: Requires two or more persons acting in agreement
The agreement alone completes the offence
Punishment is prescribed separately for conspiracies to commit serious offences

section_62.title: Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment
section_62.description: Punishes attempts to commit offences carrying life or other imprisonment, where no express provision exists: up to one-half of life imprisonment, or one-half of the longest term, and fine.
key_points: The general attempt provision
Half the punishment of the completed offence

chapter_5.title: Of Offences Against Woman and Child

section_63.title: Rape
section_63.description: Defines rape: sexual intercourse with a woman against her will, without her consent, by coercion or deceit, or when she is under eighteen years of age, among other listed circumstances.
key_points: Consent must be unequivocal, voluntary and communicated
Intercourse with a girl under eighteen is rape regardless of consent
No punishment here; punishments follow in sections 64 to 71

section_64.title: Punishment for rape
section_64.description: Punishes rape with rigorous imprisonment of not less than ten years, which may extend to life, and fine. Aggravated forms, such as by police officers, public servants, armed forces personnel or hospital staff, carry the same minimum.
key_points: Minimum ten years rigorous imprisonment
Covers rape by persons in positions of authority
Fine is mandatory in addition to imprisonment

section_65.title: Punishment for rape in certain cases
section_65.description: Prescribes higher punishment for rape of younger victims: rape of a woman under sixteen carries rigorous imprisonment of not less than twenty years up to life, and rape of a girl under twelve carries death or rigorous imprisonment of not less than twenty years up to life, with fine.
key_points: Under sixteen: minimum twenty years to life
Under twelve: death or minimum twenty years to life

section_66.title: Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim
section_66.description: Where rape causes the death of the victim or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state, the punishment is rigorous imprisonment of not less than twenty years up to life, or death.
key_points: Among the gravest punishments in the Sanhita

section_67.title: Sexual intercourse by husband upon his wife during separation
section_67.description: Punishes sexual intercourse by a husband with his wife during separation without her consent: two to seven years imprisonment and fine.
key_points: Applies whether the separation is judicial or otherwise

section_68.title: Sexual intercourse by a person in authority
section_68.description: Punishes sexual intercourse by a person in a position of authority, such as a jail, hospital or institutional head, who abuses that position: five to ten years rigorous imprisonment and fine.
key_points: Consent is no defence where authority is abused

section_69.title: Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means, etc.
section_69.description: A new offence: sexual intercourse obtained by deceitful means, such as a false promise of marriage, without any intent to fulfil it. Punishable with up to ten years imprisonment and fine.
key_points: New provision with no IPC equivalent
Targets false promises of marriage used to obtain consent

section_70.title: Gang rape
section_70.description: Punishes gang rape with rigorous imprisonment of not less than twenty years up to life, and fine. Where the victim is under eighteen, the punishment is life imprisonment or death.
key_points: Minimum twenty years for adult victims
Life or death where the victim is under eighteen

section_71.title: Punishment for repeat offenders
section_71.description: Punishes repeat offenders previously convicted under the serious sexual offence provisions with imprisonment for life or death.
key_points: Life or death for habitual offenders

section_72.title: Disclosure of identity of victim of certain offences, etc.
section_72.description: Punishes disclosure of the identity of a victim of sexual offences, including printing or publishing her name or identifying details: up to two years, or fine, or both.
key_points: Protects victim anonymity
Exceptions only as permitted by law

section_73.title: Printing or publishing any matter relating to Court proceedings without permission
section_73.description: Punishes printing or publishing any matter relating to court proceedings in sexual offence cases without the court's prior permission: up to two years and fine.

section_74.title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
section_74.description: Punishes assault or criminal force used against a woman intending to outrage her modesty: not less than one year up to five years, and fine.
key_points: Minimum one year imprisonment

section_75.title: Sexual harassment
section_75.description: Punishes sexual harassment: unwelcome physical contact, demands for sexual favours, or showing pornography carry up to three years; sexually coloured remarks carry up to one year, with fine.
key_points: Graded punishment for three forms of harassment

section_76.title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe
section_76.description: Punishes assault or criminal force against a woman with intent to disrobe her: three to seven years and fine.

section_77.title: Voyeurism
section_77.description: Punishes voyeurism, watching or capturing a woman in a private act without consent: one to three years plus fine for a first offence, and three to seven years plus fine on repeat conviction.
key_points: Higher punishment for repeat offenders

section_78.title: Stalking
section_78.description: Punishes stalking, following or monitoring a woman despite her disinterest, or contacting her online repeatedly: up to three years plus fine first time, and up to five years plus fine on repeat.
key_points: Covers both physical and electronic stalking

section_79.title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty of a woman
section_79.description: Punishes any word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_80.title: Dowry death
section_80.description: Punishes dowry death, where a woman dies from burns or bodily injury within seven years of marriage amid cruelty for dowry: not less than seven years up to life imprisonment.
key_points: Minimum seven years
Applies to deaths within seven years of marriage linked to dowry demands

section_81.title: Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage
section_81.description: Punishes a man who deceitfully induces a woman who is not his wife to believe she is lawfully married to him and cohabits with her: up to ten years and fine.

section_82.title: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife
section_82.description: Punishes marrying again during the lifetime of a husband or wife: up to seven years and fine, rising to ten years where the second marriage is concealed from the new spouse.
key_points: Concealment of the earlier marriage doubles the maximum

section_83.title: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage
section_83.description: Punishes going through a marriage ceremony fraudulently, knowing there is no lawful marriage: up to seven years and fine.

section_84.title: Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman
section_84.description: Punishes enticing, taking away or detaining a married woman with criminal intent: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_85.title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
section_85.description: Punishes a husband or his relative who subjects a woman to cruelty: up to three years and fine.
key_points: The former IPC 498A offence
Covers physical and mental cruelty including dowry harassment

section_86.title: Cruelty defined
section_86.description: Defines cruelty for section 85: wilful conduct likely to drive a woman to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to coerce her or her family over unlawful demands for property.
key_points: No separate punishment; supports section 85

section_87.title: Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc.
section_87.description: Punishes kidnapping, abducting or inducing a woman to compel her marriage or illicit intercourse: up to ten years and fine.

section_88.title: Causing miscarriage
section_88.description: Punishes voluntarily causing miscarriage: up to three years, or fine, or both, rising to seven years and fine where the woman is quick with child. Done in good faith to save her life, it is no offence.
key_points: Higher punishment where the woman is quick with child
Good-faith acts to save her life are exempt

section_89.title: Causing miscarriage without woman's consent
section_89.description: Punishes causing miscarriage without the woman's consent: up to ten years or life imprisonment, and fine.

section_90.title: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
section_90.description: Where death results from an act done with intent to cause miscarriage, the punishment is up to ten years and fine, or life imprisonment where it was done without the woman's consent.

section_91.title: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause to die after birth
section_91.description: Punishes doing any act with intent to prevent a child being born alive, or to cause it to die after birth: up to ten years, or fine, or both, unless done in good faith to save the mother's life.

section_92.title: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide
section_92.description: Punishes causing the death of a quick unborn child by an act amounting to culpable homicide: up to ten years and fine.

section_93.title: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it
section_93.description: Punishes a parent or caregiver who exposes or abandons a child under twelve: up to seven years, or fine, or both.

section_94.title: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body
section_94.description: Punishes concealment of a birth by secretly disposing of the dead body of a child: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_95.title: Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence
section_95.description: A new offence: hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence. Punishable with not less than three years up to ten years and fine.
key_points: New provision with no IPC equivalent
Minimum three years imprisonment

section_96.title: Procuration of child
section_96.description: Punishes inducing a girl under eighteen or a boy under sixteen to go anywhere for illicit intercourse: up to ten years and fine.

section_97.title: Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person
section_97.description: Punishes kidnapping or abducting a child under ten with intent to steal from its person: up to seven years and fine.

section_98.title: Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
section_98.description: Punishes selling a child for prostitution or illicit intercourse: not less than ten years up to life, and fine.
key_points: Minimum ten years

section_99.title: Buying child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
section_99.description: Punishes buying a child for prostitution or illicit intercourse: seven to fourteen years and fine.

chapter_6.title: Of Offences Affecting the Human Body

section_100.title: Culpable homicide
section_100.description: Defines culpable homicide: causing death by an act done with the intention of causing death, with the intention of causing bodily injury likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that death is likely.
key_points: The genus; murder in section 101 is its gravest species
No punishment here; punishments follow in sections 103 to 106

section_101.title: Murder
section_101.description: Defines murder: culpable homicide becomes murder when done with intention to cause death, with intention to cause injury the offender knows is likely to cause death, with intention to cause injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, or with knowledge that the act is imminently dangerous.
key_points: Four clauses marking out murder from culpable homicide
Five exceptions reduce murder to culpable homicide not amounting to murder

section_102.title: Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended
section_102.description: Where death is caused to a different person than intended, the offender is liable for culpable homicide as if he had caused the death of his intended victim.
key_points: Transferred malice: intent follows the act

section_103.title: Punishment for murder
section_103.description: Punishes murder with death or life imprisonment, and fine. Murder committed by a group of five or more persons acting together on grounds such as race, caste, sex, language or belief carries the same punishment.
key_points: Death or life imprisonment, plus fine
Group-of-five identity-based killing (mob lynching) is expressly covered
The former IPC 302 offence

section_104.title: Punishment for murder by life-convict
section_104.description: Punishes murder committed by a person already under sentence of life imprisonment with death or life imprisonment, and fine.

section_105.title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
section_105.description: Punishes culpable homicide not amounting to murder: life imprisonment or up to ten years and fine where done with intention or knowledge, and up to ten years or fine or both where done without such intention.
key_points: Two grades based on intention or knowledge

section_106.title: Causing death by negligence
section_106.description: Punishes causing death by a rash or negligent act: up to five years and fine. Causing death by rash and negligent driving and escaping without reporting it carries up to ten years and fine.
key_points: Five years for ordinary negligence
Up to ten years for hit-and-run driving deaths
Registered medical practitioners acting negligently face up to two years

section_107.title: Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind
section_107.description: Punishes abetment of suicide of a child, a person of unsound mind, or an intoxicated person: death, life imprisonment, or up to ten years, and fine.

section_108.title: Abetment of suicide
section_108.description: Punishes abetment of suicide: up to ten years and fine.

section_109.title: Attempt to murder
section_109.description: Punishes attempt to murder: up to ten years and fine, rising to life imprisonment where hurt is caused.
key_points: Life imprisonment if the attempt causes hurt

section_110.title: Attempt to commit culpable homicide
section_110.description: Punishes attempt to commit culpable homicide not amounting to murder: up to three years or fine, rising to seven years where hurt is caused.

section_111.title: Organised crime
section_111.description: A new offence covering organised crime by a continuing unlawful syndicate, such as kidnapping for ransom, contract killing, extortion or cybercrime rings. Where death results: death or life; otherwise not less than five years up to life, plus fine of at least five lakh rupees.
key_points: New provision with no IPC equivalent
Minimum five years where no death is caused
Minimum fine of five lakh rupees

section_112.title: Petty organised crime
section_112.description: A new offence covering petty organised crime by groups acting in concert, such as theft, cheating, or pickpocketing gangs: not less than one year up to seven years and fine.
key_points: New provision with no IPC equivalent

section_113.title: Terrorist act
section_113.description: A new offence defining a terrorist act: acts done with intent to threaten India's unity, integrity, security or sovereignty, or to strike terror. Where death results: death or life; otherwise not less than five years up to life, and fine.
key_points: New provision with no IPC equivalent
Covers bombings, hostage-taking and attacks on public functionaries

section_114.title: Hurt
section_114.description: Defines hurt as bodily pain, disease or infirmity caused to any person.
key_points: No punishment here; punishments follow in sections 115 to 125

section_115.title: Voluntarily causing hurt
section_115.description: Punishes voluntarily causing hurt: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_116.title: Grievous hurt
section_116.description: Defines grievous hurt through eight listed kinds, including emasculation, permanent loss of sight or hearing, fracture, and hurt endangering life or causing twenty days of severe pain.
key_points: Eight specific kinds of grievous hurt
No punishment here; punishments follow in sections 117 to 124

section_117.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
section_117.description: Punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt: up to seven years and fine.

section_118.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
section_118.description: Punishes voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means: up to three years for hurt, and life imprisonment or up to ten years for grievous hurt, with fine.
key_points: Life imprisonment possible for grievous hurt with weapons

section_119.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act
section_119.description: Punishes causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property or constrain a person to an illegal act: up to ten years and fine, or life imprisonment where grievous hurt is caused.

section_120.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property
section_120.description: Punishes causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort a confession or compel restoration of property: up to seven years and fine, or up to ten years where grievous hurt is caused.

section_121.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty
section_121.description: Punishes voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter a public servant from duty: up to three years for hurt and up to ten years for grievous hurt, with fine.

section_122.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation
section_122.description: Provides lighter punishment for hurt or grievous hurt caused on grave and sudden provocation, where the offender neither intended nor knew the harm was likely.
key_points: Provocation must be grave, sudden, and not sought by the offender

section_123.title: Causing hurt by means of poison, etc., with intent to commit an offence
section_123.description: Punishes causing hurt by poison or stupefying drugs with intent to commit an offence: up to ten years and fine.

section_124.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, etc.
section_124.description: Punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt by acid: not less than ten years up to life and fine, with compensation to the victim. Throwing or attempting to throw acid carries five to seven years and fine.
key_points: Minimum ten years for acid attacks causing grievous hurt
Fine must help meet the victim's medical expenses

section_125.title: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
section_125.description: Punishes rash or negligent acts endangering life or personal safety, graded from up to three months where no harm results to up to three years where grievous hurt results.
key_points: Punishment rises with the harm actually caused

section_126.title: Wrongful restraint
section_126.description: Defines wrongful restraint, obstructing a person from proceeding in a direction they have a right to go, and punishes it with up to one month, or fine, or both.

section_127.title: Wrongful confinement
section_127.description: Defines wrongful confinement, keeping a person within limits they cannot leave, and punishes it with up to one year or fine or both, rising to two years for three or more days and three years for ten or more days.
key_points: Punishment rises with the length of confinement

section_128.title: Force
section_128.description: Defines force as causing motion, change of motion, or cessation of motion to another person or thing.
key_points: A definitional building block for criminal force and assault

section_129.title: Criminal force
section_129.description: Defines criminal force: intentionally using force against a person without consent, in order to commit an offence or with intent to cause injury, fear or annoyance.

section_130.title: Assault
section_130.description: Defines assault as a gesture or preparation intending or known to be likely to cause apprehension that criminal force will be used.
key_points: Apprehension of force is enough; no touching needed

section_131.title: Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation
section_131.description: Punishes assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation: up to three months, or fine, or both.

section_132.title: Assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty
section_132.description: Punishes assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from duty: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_133.title: Assault or criminal force with intent to dishonour person, otherwise than on grave provocation
section_133.description: Punishes assault or criminal force with intent to dishonour a person, otherwise than on grave provocation: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_134.title: Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person
section_134.description: Punishes assault or criminal force in an attempt to commit theft of property worn or carried by a person: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_135.title: Assault or criminal force in attempt to wrongfully confine a person
section_135.description: Punishes assault or criminal force in an attempt to wrongfully confine a person: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_136.title: Assault or criminal force on grave provocation
section_136.description: Provides lighter punishment for assault or criminal force on grave and sudden provocation: up to one month, or fine, or both.

section_137.title: Kidnapping
section_137.description: Defines kidnapping: taking or enticing a child under eighteen, or a person of unsound mind, out of lawful guardianship, or taking a person by force or deceit from India or lawful guardianship.
key_points: Two kinds: from India, and from lawful guardianship

section_138.title: Abduction
section_138.description: Defines abduction: compelling or inducing a person by force or deceit to go from any place.
key_points: Force or deceit is essential; age is irrelevant unlike kidnapping

section_139.title: Kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging
section_139.description: Punishes kidnapping or maiming a child for begging: not less than ten years up to life, and life where the child is maimed.
key_points: Minimum ten years

section_140.title: Kidnapping or abducting in order to murder or for ransom, etc.
section_140.description: Punishes kidnapping or abducting in order to murder or for ransom: up to life and fine, or death or life and fine where ransom is demanded with threat of death or hurt.
key_points: Death penalty possible in ransom cases with threats

section_141.title: Importation of girl or boy from foreign country
section_141.description: Punishes importing a girl under twenty-one or a boy under eighteen from a foreign country for illicit intercourse: up to ten years and fine.

section_142.title: Wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement, kidnapped or abducted person
section_142.description: Punishes wrongfully concealing or confining a kidnapped or abducted person: the same punishment as for the kidnapping or abduction itself.

section_143.title: Trafficking of person
section_143.description: Punishes trafficking of persons for exploitation: seven years to life, and ten years to life on repeat conviction.
key_points: Minimum seven years
Covers recruitment, transport and harbouring for exploitation

section_144.title: Exploitation of a trafficked person
section_144.description: Punishes sexual exploitation of a trafficked person: five years to life and fine.

section_145.title: Habitual dealing in slaves
section_145.description: Punishes habitual dealing in slaves: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_146.title: Unlawful compulsory labour
section_146.description: Punishes compelling any person to labour against his will: up to one year, or fine, or both.
key_points: Covers bonded and forced labour

section_147.title: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against Government of India
section_147.description: Punishes waging war, attempting to wage war, or abetting the waging of war against the Government of India: death or life imprisonment, and fine.
key_points: The gravest offence against the State

section_148.title: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147
section_148.description: Punishes conspiracy to commit offences punishable under section 147: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_149.title: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against Government of India
section_149.description: Punishes collecting arms or ammunition with the intention of waging war against the Government of India: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_150.title: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
section_150.description: Punishes concealing, with intent to facilitate, a design to wage war: up to ten years and fine.

section_151.title: Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain exercise of any lawful power
section_151.description: Punishes assaulting the President, a Governor, or similar dignitary with intent to compel or restrain lawful power: up to seven years and fine.

section_152.title: Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
section_152.description: Punishes acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India, including secessionist, separatist and armed-rebellion activity and aiding a foreign power: life imprisonment or up to seven years, and fine.
key_points: New provision with no IPC equivalent
Replaces the colonial sedition offence with a narrower sovereignty offence
Never to be labelled sedition

section_153.title: Waging war against Government of any foreign State at peace with Government of India
section_153.description: Punishes waging war against the government of a foreign state at peace with India: life imprisonment or up to seven years, and fine.

section_154.title: Committing depredation on territories of foreign State at peace with Government of India
section_154.description: Punishes committing depredation on the territory of a friendly foreign state: up to seven years, and fine and forfeiture of property used.

section_155.title: Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 153 and 154
section_155.description: Punishes receiving property taken by such war or depredation, knowing it was so taken: up to seven years, and fine and forfeiture.

section_156.title: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape
section_156.description: Punishes a public servant who voluntarily allows a State prisoner or prisoner of war to escape: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_157.title: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape
section_157.description: Punishes a public servant who negligently suffers such a prisoner to escape: up to three years and fine.

section_158.title: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner
section_158.description: Punishes aiding the escape of, rescuing, or harbouring such a prisoner: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

chapter_8.title: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force

section_159.title: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty
section_159.description: Punishes abetting mutiny or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from duty: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_160.title: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof
section_160.description: Where mutiny is committed in consequence of such abetment, the punishment is death, life imprisonment, or up to ten years, and fine.

section_161.title: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office
section_161.description: Punishes abetment of assault by a soldier, sailor or airman on a superior officer in execution of office: up to three years and fine.

section_162.title: Abetment of such assault, if assault committed
section_162.description: Where such assault is committed in consequence of the abetment, the punishment is up to seven years and fine.

section_163.title: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
section_163.description: Punishes abetment of desertion of a soldier, sailor or airman: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_164.title: Harbouring deserter
section_164.description: Punishes harbouring a deserter, knowing or having reason to believe he has deserted: up to two years, or fine, or both.
key_points: The wife's harbouring of a husband is excepted

section_165.title: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
section_165.description: Punishes the master of a merchant vessel who negligently allows a concealed deserter on board: up to one year or fine, unless he had no reason to believe it.

section_166.title: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman
section_166.description: Punishes abetment of an act of insubordination by a soldier, sailor or airman: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_167.title: Persons subject to certain Acts
section_167.description: Provides that persons subject to the Army, Navy or Air Force Acts are not punishable under the Sanhita for acts which are offences under those Acts.

section_168.title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
section_168.description: Punishes wearing military garb or carrying a token used by a soldier, sailor or airman with intent that it be believed he holds that rank: up to three months, or fine, or both.

section_169.title: Candidate, electoral right defined
section_169.description: Defines candidate and electoral right for the election offences in this Chapter.

section_170.title: Bribery
section_170.description: Defines bribery at elections: giving or offering gratification to induce voting, or receiving it for voting or refraining.

section_171.title: Undue influence at elections
section_171.description: Defines undue influence at elections: voluntary interference with the free exercise of an electoral right, including threats of injury.
key_points: Threatening divine displeasure counts as interference

section_172.title: Personation at elections
section_172.description: Defines personation at elections: voting or applying for a ballot paper in another person's name, living or dead, or under a fictitious name.

section_173.title: Punishment for bribery
section_173.description: Punishes bribery at elections: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_174.title: Punishment for undue influence or personation at an election
section_174.description: Punishes undue influence or personation at an election: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_175.title: False statement in connection with an election
section_175.description: Punishes making or publishing a false statement about a candidate's personal character or conduct to affect the election: fine.

section_176.title: Illegal payments in connection with an election
section_176.description: Punishes illegal payments in connection with an election, made without the candidate's authority: fine.

section_177.title: Failure to keep election accounts
section_177.description: Punishes failure to keep election accounts as required by law: fine.

chapter_10.title: Of Offences Relating to Coin, Currency-Notes, Bank-Notes, and Government Stamps

section_178.title: Counterfeiting coin, Government stamps, currency-notes or bank-notes
section_178.description: Punishes counterfeiting coin, Government stamps, currency-notes or bank-notes: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.
key_points: One consolidated counterfeiting provision

section_179.title: Using as genuine, forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes
section_179.description: Punishes using as genuine any forged or counterfeit coin, stamp, currency-note or bank-note, knowing it to be forged: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_180.title: Possession of forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes
section_180.description: Punishes possessing forged or counterfeit coin, stamps or notes, knowing them to be forged and intending to use them as genuine: up to seven years and fine.

section_181.title: Making or possessing instruments or materials for forging or counterfeiting coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes
section_181.description: Punishes making or possessing instruments or materials for forging or counterfeiting coin, stamps or notes: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_182.title: Making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes
section_182.description: Punishes making or using documents resembling currency-notes or bank-notes, and refusing to disclose the printer's name: fine.

section_183.title: Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government
section_183.description: Punishes effacing writing from a substance bearing a Government stamp, or removing a stamp from a document, to cause loss to Government: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_184.title: Using Government stamp known to have been before used
section_184.description: Punishes using a Government stamp known to have been used before: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_185.title: Erasure of mark denoting that stamp has been used
section_185.description: Punishes erasure of a mark denoting that a stamp has been used: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_186.title: Prohibition of fictitious stamps
section_186.description: Prohibits fictitious stamps and punishes making, selling or possessing them: fine.

section_187.title: Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law
section_187.description: Punishes a mint employee who fraudulently causes coin to differ in weight or composition from the legal standard: up to seven years and fine.

section_188.title: Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint
section_188.description: Punishes unlawfully taking a coining instrument from a mint: up to seven years and fine.

chapter_11.title: Of Offences Against the Public Tranquillity

section_189.title: Unlawful assembly
section_189.description: Defines unlawful assembly: five or more persons with a common object to commit specified wrongs, such as overawing the Government, resisting law, or committing mischief or criminal trespass.
key_points: Five or more persons with a common unlawful object

section_190.title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
section_190.description: Makes every member of an unlawful assembly guilty of any offence committed by any member in prosecution of their common object, where they knew it was likely.
key_points: Shared liability for the common object

section_191.title: Rioting
section_191.description: Defines rioting, use of force or violence by an unlawful assembly or its member, and punishes it with up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_192.title: Wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot-if rioting be committed; if not committed
section_192.description: Punishes wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause a riot: up to one year if rioting results, and up to six months where it does not.

section_193.title: Liability of owner, occupier, etc., of land on which an unlawful assembly or riot takes place
section_193.description: Makes owners or occupiers of land liable to fine where an unlawful assembly or riot takes place with their knowledge on land in their charge.

section_194.title: Affray
section_194.description: Defines affray, fighting in a public place disturbing the peace, and punishes it with up to three months, or fine, or both.

section_195.title: Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc.
section_195.description: Punishes assaulting or obstructing a public servant who is suppressing a riot or affray, or assaulting anyone aiding him: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_196.title: Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc., and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony
section_196.description: Punishes promoting enmity between groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence or language, and acts prejudicial to harmony: up to three years, or fine, or both, rising to five years on repeat.
key_points: Covers hate speech threatening communal harmony

section_197.title: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration
section_197.description: Punishes imputations or assertions prejudicial to national integration, such as claims that a community should be denied rights: up to three years, or fine, or both.

chapter_12.title: Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants

section_198.title: Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person
section_198.description: Punishes a public servant who disobeys the law with intent to cause injury to any person: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_199.title: Public servant disobeying direction under law
section_199.description: Punishes a public servant who disobeys a legal direction, such as failing to record information or act on a complaint: six months to two years and fine.
key_points: Minimum six months imprisonment

section_200.title: Punishment for non-treatment of victim
section_200.description: Punishes whoever, being in charge of a hospital, fails to provide first aid or medical treatment to a victim of specified offences: up to one year, or fine, or both.
key_points: Hospitals cannot turn away victims of sexual offences or acid attacks

section_201.title: Public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury
section_201.description: Punishes a public servant who frames an incorrect document with intent to cause injury: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_202.title: Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade
section_202.description: Punishes a public servant who unlawfully engages in trade: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_203.title: Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property
section_203.description: Punishes a public servant who unlawfully buys or bids for property: up to two years, or fine, or both, with confiscation of the property.

section_204.title: Personating a public servant
section_204.description: Punishes personating a public servant: six months to three years and fine.

section_205.title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent
section_205.description: Punishes wearing the garb or carrying the token of a public servant with fraudulent intent: up to six months, or fine, or both.

chapter_13.title: Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants

section_206.title: Absconding to avoid service of summons or other proceeding
section_206.description: Punishes absconding to avoid service of summons or other court process: up to one month or fine, rising to six months or fine where the summons relates to serious matters.

section_207.title: Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof
section_207.description: Punishes preventing the service of summons or its publication: up to one month or fine, rising to six months or fine in serious cases.

section_208.title: Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant
section_208.description: Punishes intentional non-attendance in obedience to an order from a public servant: up to one month or fine, rising to six months or fine in serious cases.

section_209.title: Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
section_209.description: Punishes non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita: up to three years and fine.

section_210.title: Omission to produce document or electronic record to public servant by person legally bound to produce it
section_210.description: Punishes intentional omission to produce a document or electronic record to a public servant by a person legally bound to produce it: up to one month or fine, rising to six months or fine.
key_points: Expressly covers electronic records

section_211.title: Omission to give notice or information to public servant by person legally bound to give it
section_211.description: Punishes intentional omission to give notice or information to a public servant by a person legally bound to give it: up to one month or fine, rising to six months or fine.

section_212.title: Furnishing false information
section_212.description: Punishes furnishing false information to a public servant: up to one month or fine, rising to six months or fine.

section_213.title: Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it
section_213.description: Punishes refusing to take an oath or affirmation when duly required by a public servant: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_214.title: Refusing to answer public servant authorised to question
section_214.description: Punishes refusing to answer a public servant authorised to question: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_215.title: Refusing to sign statement
section_215.description: Punishes refusing to sign a statement made to a public servant when legally required: fine.

section_216.title: False statement on oath or affirmation to public servant or person authorised to administer an oath or affirmation
section_216.description: Punishes making a false statement on oath or affirmation to a public servant or person authorised to administer it: up to three years and fine.
key_points: Perjury before public servants, distinct from false evidence in court

section_217.title: False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person
section_217.description: Punishes giving false information with intent to cause a public servant to use lawful power to injure another: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_218.title: Resistance to taking of property by lawful authority of a public servant
section_218.description: Punishes resistance to the taking of property by the lawful authority of a public servant: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_219.title: Obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant
section_219.description: Punishes intentionally obstructing the sale of property offered for sale by a public servant's authority: up to one month, or fine, or both.

section_220.title: Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant
section_220.description: Punishes illegal purchase or bidding for property offered for sale by a public servant's authority: up to one month, or fine, or both.

section_221.title: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions
section_221.description: Punishes obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions: up to three months, or fine, or both.

section_222.title: Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance
section_222.description: Punishes omission to assist a public servant when bound by law to give assistance: up to one month or fine, rising to six months or fine.

section_223.title: Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant
section_223.description: Punishes disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant: up to six months or fine where no danger results, and up to one year or fine where danger to human life, health or safety results.
key_points: Higher punishment where disobedience endangers life or safety

section_224.title: Threat of injury to public servant
section_224.description: Punishes threatening injury to a public servant to deter him from duty: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_225.title: Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant
section_225.description: Punishes threatening injury to induce a person to refrain from seeking protection from a public servant: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_226.title: Attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power
section_226.description: Punishes attempting suicide to compel or restrain the exercise of lawful power: up to one year simple imprisonment, or fine, or both, or community service.
key_points: Attempting suicide itself is no longer an offence under BNS
Only attempts meant to coerce public authorities are punished
Community service is an available sentence

chapter_14.title: Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice

section_227.title: Giving false evidence
section_227.description: Defines giving false evidence: making a false statement on oath, or in a declaration the law treats as evidence, which the person knows or believes to be false.

section_228.title: Fabricating false evidence
section_228.description: Defines fabricating false evidence: causing circumstances to exist or making false entries with intent that they appear in judicial proceedings as genuine.

section_229.title: Punishment for false evidence
section_229.description: Punishes giving or fabricating false evidence: up to seven years and fine, or life imprisonment or up to ten years where committed in a judicial proceeding.
key_points: Life imprisonment possible for perjury in judicial proceedings

section_230.title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence
section_230.description: Where false evidence is given to procure conviction for a capital offence, the punishment is life imprisonment or up to ten years and fine, or death or life where an innocent person is executed in consequence.
key_points: Death penalty possible where an innocent person is executed

section_231.title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment
section_231.description: Where false evidence is given to procure conviction for an offence punishable with life or other imprisonment, the punishment matches that offence, and may extend to life imprisonment.

section_232.title: Threatening any person to give false evidence
section_232.description: Punishes threatening any person to give false evidence: up to seven years, or fine, or both.

section_233.title: Using evidence known to be false
section_233.description: Punishes corruptly using or attempting to use as true any evidence known to be false: the same punishment as for giving false evidence.

section_234.title: Issuing or signing false certificate
section_234.description: Punishes issuing or signing a false certificate: up to seven years and fine.

section_235.title: Using as true a certificate known to be false
section_235.description: Punishes using as true a certificate known to be false: the same punishment as for issuing it.

section_236.title: False statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence
section_236.description: Punishes making a false statement in a declaration receivable as evidence: up to three years and fine.

section_237.title: Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false
section_237.description: Punishes corruptly using as true such a declaration knowing it to be false: the same punishment.

section_238.title: Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender
section_238.description: Punishes causing disappearance of evidence of an offence, or giving false information to screen the offender: graded up to seven years and fine for the gravest offences.
key_points: Punishment scales with the gravity of the offence concealed

section_239.title: Intentional omission to give information of offence by person bound to inform
section_239.description: Punishes intentional omission to give information of an offence by a person bound to inform: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_240.title: Giving false information respecting an offence committed
section_240.description: Punishes giving false information about an offence committed: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_241.title: Destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence
section_241.description: Punishes destroying a document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence: up to two years, or fine, or both.
key_points: Expressly covers electronic records

section_242.title: False personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution
section_242.description: Punishes false personation for the purpose of any act or proceeding in a suit or prosecution: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_243.title: Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
section_243.description: Punishes fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_244.title: Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution
section_244.description: Punishes fraudulently claiming property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_245.title: Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due
section_245.description: Punishes fraudulently suffering a decree for a sum not due: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_246.title: Dishonestly making false claim in Court
section_246.description: Punishes dishonestly making a false claim in court: up to two years and fine.

section_247.title: Fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due
section_247.description: Punishes fraudulently obtaining a decree for a sum not due: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_248.title: False charge of offence made with intent to injure
section_248.description: Punishes instituting false criminal proceedings with intent to injure: up to two years, or fine, or both, rising to seven years where the false charge is of an offence punishable with death or life.

section_249.title: Harbouring offender
section_249.description: Punishes harbouring an offender with intent to screen him from punishment: graded up to five years and fine for the gravest offences.
key_points: Punishment scales with the harboured offence

section_250.title: Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment
section_250.description: Punishes taking a gift or gratification to screen an offender from punishment: graded up to seven years for capital offences.

section_251.title: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender
section_251.description: Punishes offering a gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening an offender: graded up to seven years for capital offences.

section_252.title: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.
section_252.description: Punishes taking a gift to help recover stolen property without using lawful means: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_253.title: Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered
section_253.description: Punishes harbouring an offender who has escaped custody or whose apprehension is ordered: graded up to seven years for capital offences.

section_254.title: Penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits
section_254.description: Punishes harbouring robbers or dacoits: up to seven years and fine.

section_255.title: Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture
section_255.description: Punishes a public servant who disobeys the law with intent to save a person from punishment or property from forfeiture: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_256.title: Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture
section_256.description: Punishes a public servant who frames an incorrect record or writing with such intent: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_257.title: Public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report, etc., contrary to law
section_257.description: Punishes a public servant who in a judicial proceeding corruptly makes an order or report contrary to law: up to seven years, or fine, or both.

section_258.title: Commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting contrary to law
section_258.description: Punishes a person in authority who, knowing he acts contrary to law, commits a person for trial or confinement: up to seven years, or fine, or both.

section_259.title: Intentional omission to apprehend on part of public servant bound to apprehend
section_259.description: Punishes a public servant bound to apprehend who intentionally omits to do so: graded up to seven years.

section_260.title: Intentional omission to apprehend on part of public servant bound to apprehend person under sentence or lawfully committed
section_260.description: Where the person to be apprehended is under sentence or lawfully committed, such intentional omission carries life imprisonment or up to ten years.

section_261.title: Escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant
section_261.description: Punishes a public servant who negligently suffers an escape from confinement or custody: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_262.title: Resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension
section_262.description: Punishes resistance or obstruction by a person to his own lawful apprehension: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_263.title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person
section_263.description: Punishes resistance or obstruction to the lawful apprehension of another person: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_264.title: Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for
section_264.description: Punishes a public servant's omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, in cases not otherwise provided for: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_265.title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension or escape or rescue in cases not otherwise provided for
section_265.description: Punishes resistance, obstruction, escape or rescue in cases not otherwise provided for: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_266.title: Violation of condition of remission of punishment
section_266.description: Punishes violation of a condition of remission of punishment: the unexpired punishment, or up to two years where the original punishment was remitted.

section_267.title: Intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding
section_267.description: Punishes intentional insult or interruption to a public servant sitting in a judicial proceeding: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_268.title: Personation of assessor
section_268.description: Punishes personation of an assessor: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_269.title: Failure by person released on bail bond or bond to appear in Court
section_269.description: Punishes failure by a person released on bail bond or bond to appear in court: up to one year, or fine, or both.
key_points: Jumping bail is itself an offence

chapter_15.title: Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals

section_270.title: Public nuisance
section_270.description: Defines public nuisance: any act or illegal omission causing common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or people in general.
key_points: No punishment here; punishments follow in sections 271 to 297

section_271.title: Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life
section_271.description: Punishes negligently doing an act known to be likely to spread infection of a dangerous disease: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_272.title: Malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life
section_272.description: Punishes malignantly doing such an act, with deliberate intent to spread the infection: up to two years, or fine, or both.
key_points: Deliberate spreading carries four times the negligent maximum

section_273.title: Disobedience to quarantine rule
section_273.description: Punishes knowingly disobeying a quarantine rule laid down by the Government: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_274.title: Adulteration of food or drink intended for sale
section_274.description: Punishes adulteration of food or drink intended for sale, making it noxious: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_275.title: Sale of noxious food or drink
section_275.description: Punishes selling noxious food or drink, knowing it to be noxious: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_276.title: Adulteration of drugs
section_276.description: Punishes adulteration of drugs or medical preparations, lessening their efficacy or making them noxious: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_277.title: Sale of adulterated drugs
section_277.description: Punishes knowingly selling adulterated drugs: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_278.title: Sale of drug as a different drug or preparation
section_278.description: Punishes selling a drug as a different drug or preparation: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_279.title: Fouling water of public spring or reservoir
section_279.description: Punishes voluntarily fouling the water of a public spring or reservoir: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_280.title: Making atmosphere noxious to health
section_280.description: Punishes voluntarily making the atmosphere noxious to the health of people in the neighbourhood: fine.

section_281.title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
section_281.description: Punishes rash driving or riding on a public way: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_282.title: Rash navigation of vessel
section_282.description: Punishes rash navigation of a vessel: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_283.title: Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy
section_283.description: Punishes exhibiting a false light, mark or buoy with intent to mislead navigators: up to seven years, or fine, or both.

section_284.title: Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel
section_284.description: Punishes conveying persons by water for hire in an unsafe or overloaded vessel: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_285.title: Danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation
section_285.description: Punishes causing danger or obstruction in a public way or line of navigation: fine.

section_286.title: Negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance
section_286.description: Punishes negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substances: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_287.title: Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter
section_287.description: Punishes negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter: up to six months, or fine, or both.
