section_288.title: Negligent conduct with respect to explosive substance
section_288.description: Punishes negligent conduct with respect to explosive substances: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_289.title: Negligent conduct with respect to machinery
section_289.description: Punishes negligent conduct with respect to machinery: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_290.title: Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings, etc.
section_290.description: Punishes negligent conduct in pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_291.title: Negligent conduct with respect to animal
section_291.description: Punishes negligent conduct with respect to animals, knowing the animal is likely to cause danger: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_292.title: Punishment for public nuisance in cases not otherwise provided for
section_292.description: Provides the residuary punishment for public nuisance not otherwise provided for: fine.

section_293.title: Continuance of nuisance after injunction to discontinue
section_293.description: Punishes continuing a nuisance after an injunction to discontinue: up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_294.title: Sale, etc., of obscene books, etc.
section_294.description: Punishes sale and distribution of obscene books and material: up to two years and fine first time, and up to five years and fine on repeat.
key_points: Higher punishment on repeat conviction

section_295.title: Sale, etc., of obscene objects to child
section_295.description: Punishes sale of obscene objects to a child: up to three years and fine first time, and up to seven years and fine on repeat.

section_296.title: Obscene acts and songs
section_296.description: Punishes obscene acts and songs in or near public places: up to three months, or fine, or both.

section_297.title: Keeping lottery office
section_297.description: Punishes keeping a lottery office, publishing lottery proposals, without Government authority: up to six months, or fine, or both.
key_points: Only State-authorised lotteries are exempt

section_298.title: Injuring or defiling place of worship with intent to insult religion of any class
section_298.description: Punishes injuring or defiling a place of worship with intent to insult the religion of any class: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_299.title: Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs
section_299.description: Punishes deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings by insulting a religion or its beliefs: up to three years, or fine, or both.
key_points: Requires deliberate and malicious intent
The former IPC 295A offence

section_300.title: Disturbing religious assembly
section_300.description: Punishes voluntarily disturbing a religious assembly: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_301.title: Trespassing on burial places, etc.
section_301.description: Punishes trespassing on burial places or places of sepulture, or indignity to a corpse: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_302.title: Uttering words, etc., with deliberate intent to wound religious feelings of any person
section_302.description: Punishes uttering words or sounds with deliberate intent to wound the religious feelings of any person: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_303.title: Theft
section_303.description: Defines theft, dishonestly moving movable property out of anyone's possession without consent, and punishes it with up to three years, or fine, or both, with enhanced punishment for repeat convictions.
key_points: Dishonest intention is essential
Only movable property can be stolen
Enhanced punishment on second or subsequent conviction
The former IPC 379 offence

section_304.title: Snatching
section_304.description: A new offence: snatching, sudden or quick or forcible seizure of property from a person. Punishable with up to three years and fine.
key_points: New provision with no IPC equivalent
Covers chain and mobile snatching

section_305.title: Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc.
section_305.description: Punishes theft in a dwelling house, tent, vessel, vehicle, or place of worship: up to seven years and fine.

section_306.title: Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master
section_306.description: Punishes theft by a clerk or servant of property in the possession of the master: up to seven years and fine.

section_307.title: Theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint in order to committing of theft
section_307.description: Punishes theft after preparation for causing death, hurt or restraint in order to commit the theft: up to ten years and fine.

section_308.title: Extortion
section_308.description: Defines extortion, putting a person in fear of injury to dishonestly induce delivery of property, and punishes it with up to seven years, or fine, or both.
key_points: Fear of injury is the essence of extortion

section_309.title: Robbery
section_309.description: Defines robbery, theft or extortion accompanied by violence or threats, and punishes it with rigorous imprisonment up to ten years and fine, rising to fourteen years for robbery on the highway between sunset and sunrise.
key_points: Theft becomes robbery when force or fear is used
Higher punishment for highway robbery at night

section_310.title: Dacoity
section_310.description: Defines dacoity, robbery committed by five or more persons conjointly, and punishes it with life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.
key_points: Five or more persons acting together make it dacoity

section_311.title: Robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
section_311.description: Where robbery or dacoity is committed with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt, the punishment is not less than seven years.
key_points: Minimum seven years

section_312.title: Attempt to commit robbery or dacoity when armed with deadly weapon
section_312.description: Punishes attempt to commit robbery or dacoity when armed with a deadly weapon: not less than seven years.

section_313.title: Punishment for belonging to gang of robbers, etc.
section_313.description: Punishes belonging to a gang of persons associated for habitually committing robbery or dacoity: up to seven years and fine.

section_314.title: Dishonest misappropriation of property
section_314.description: Defines dishonest misappropriation of property and punishes it with up to two years, or fine, or both.
key_points: Covers finding and keeping lost property dishonestly

section_315.title: Dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person at the time of his death
section_315.description: Punishes dishonest misappropriation of property known to have belonged to a deceased person: up to three years and fine.

section_316.title: Criminal breach of trust
section_316.description: Defines criminal breach of trust and punishes it with up to five years or fine or both, rising to seven years for carriers, warehouse-keepers, clerks and servants, and to life or ten years for public servants, bankers and agents.
key_points: Punishment rises with the offender's position of trust
The former IPC 409 offence for public servants carries life or ten years

section_317.title: Stolen property
section_317.description: Defines stolen property and punishes receiving or retaining it knowing it to be stolen: up to three years, rising to life or ten years where it belongs to dacoity or habitual dealing.

section_318.title: Cheating
section_318.description: Defines cheating, deceiving a person to fraudulently or dishonestly induce delivery of property or consent, and punishes it with up to three years, or fine, or both. Where the cheating dishonestly induces delivery of property, the punishment is up to seven years and fine.
key_points: Deception causing wrongful loss is the core
Cheating inducing delivery of property: up to seven years
The former IPC 420 offence

section_319.title: Cheating by personation
section_319.description: Punishes cheating by personation, pretending to be someone else: up to five years, or fine, or both.

section_320.title: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors
section_320.description: Punishes dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its distribution among creditors: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_321.title: Dishonestly or fraudulently preventing debt being available for creditors
section_321.description: Punishes dishonestly or fraudulently preventing a debt from being available to creditors: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_322.title: Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration
section_322.description: Punishes dishonest or fraudulent execution of a deed of transfer containing a false statement of consideration: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_323.title: Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property
section_323.description: Punishes dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_324.title: Mischief
section_324.description: Defines mischief, causing wrongful loss or damage to property, and punishes it with up to six months, or fine, or both.

section_325.title: Mischief by killing or maiming animal
section_325.description: Punishes mischief by killing, poisoning or maiming an animal: up to five years, or fine, or both.

section_326.title: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc.
section_326.description: Punishes mischief by fire, explosive substance or inundation: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_327.title: Mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a rail, aircraft, decked vessel or one of twenty tons burden
section_327.description: Punishes mischief with intent to destroy or make unsafe a rail, aircraft, or decked vessel: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_328.title: Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc.
section_328.description: Punishes intentionally running a vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft or dishonestly: up to ten years and fine.

section_329.title: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
section_329.description: Defines criminal trespass, entering property with intent to commit an offence or intimidate, and house-trespass, entering a dwelling or building used for human dwelling or worship.
key_points: No punishment here; punishments follow in sections 331 to 333

section_330.title: House-trespass and house-breaking
section_330.description: Defines house-trespass and house-breaking, entry effected by force, scaling, or other listed means, including lurking house-trespass by night.

section_331.title: Punishment for house-trespass or house-breaking
section_331.description: Punishes house-trespass or house-breaking: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_332.title: House-trespass in order to commit offence
section_332.description: Punishes house-trespass in order to commit an offence: up to seven years, rising to ten years for theft and to life or ten years where the offence is punishable with death or life.
key_points: Punishment scales with the intended offence

section_333.title: House-trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint
section_333.description: Punishes house-trespass after preparation for causing hurt, assault or wrongful restraint: up to ten years and fine, with higher punishment at night.

section_334.title: Dishonestly breaking open receptacle containing property
section_334.description: Punishes dishonestly breaking open a receptacle containing property: up to two years, or fine, or both.

chapter_18.title: Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks

section_335.title: Making a false document
section_335.description: Defines making a false document: making, signing or altering a document or electronic record dishonestly or fraudulently with intent to cause wrongful gain or loss.
key_points: Expressly covers electronic records
The foundation of all forgery offences

section_336.title: Forgery
section_336.description: Defines forgery and punishes it with up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_337.title: Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc.
section_337.description: Punishes forgery of a court record, public register, or birth, marriage or power-of-attorney document: life imprisonment or up to seven years, and fine.

section_338.title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc.
section_338.description: Punishes forgery of a valuable security, will, or authority to adopt a son: life imprisonment or up to ten years, and fine.

section_339.title: Having possession of document described in section 337 or section 338, knowing it to be forged and intending to use it as genuine
section_339.description: Punishes possessing a forged document of the kind in sections 337 or 338, knowing it to be forged and intending to use it as genuine: life imprisonment or up to seven or ten years respectively.

section_340.title: Forged document or electronic record and using it as genuine
section_340.description: Punishes fraudulently or dishonestly using as genuine a forged document or electronic record: the same punishment as for the forgery itself.

section_341.title: Making or possessing counterfeit seal, etc., with intent to commit forgery punishable under section 338
section_341.description: Punishes making or possessing a counterfeit seal or plate with intent to commit forgery punishable under section 338: life imprisonment or up to seven years, and fine.

section_342.title: Counterfeiting device or mark used for authenticating documents described in section 338, or possessing counterfeit marked material
section_342.description: Punishes counterfeiting a device or mark used to authenticate section 338 documents, or possessing counterfeit marked material: life imprisonment or up to seven years, and fine.

section_343.title: Fraudulent cancellation, destruction, etc., of will, authority to adopt, or valuable security
section_343.description: Punishes fraudulent cancellation or destruction of a will, authority to adopt, or valuable security: life imprisonment or up to seven years, and fine.

section_344.title: Falsification of accounts
section_344.description: Punishes falsification of accounts by a clerk, officer or servant: up to seven years, or fine, or both.

section_345.title: Property mark
section_345.description: Defines property mark: a mark denoting that goods belong to a particular person.

section_346.title: Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury
section_346.description: Punishes tampering with a property mark with intent to cause injury: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_347.title: Counterfeiting a property mark
section_347.description: Punishes counterfeiting a property mark: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_348.title: Making or possession of any instrument for counterfeiting a property mark
section_348.description: Punishes making or possessing an instrument for counterfeiting a property mark: up to three years, or fine, or both.

section_349.title: Selling goods marked with a counterfeit property mark
section_349.description: Punishes selling goods marked with a counterfeit property mark: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_350.title: Making a false mark upon any receptacle containing goods
section_350.description: Punishes making a false mark upon a receptacle containing goods: up to three years, or fine, or both.

chapter_19.title: Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult, Annoyance, Defamation, etc.

section_351.title: Criminal intimidation
section_351.description: Defines criminal intimidation, threatening injury to person, reputation or property, and punishes it with up to two years, or fine, or both, rising to seven years where the threat is of death, grievous hurt, or arson.
key_points: Threats of death or grievous hurt: up to seven years
The former IPC 506 offence

section_352.title: Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace
section_352.description: Punishes intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace: up to two years, or fine, or both.

section_353.title: Statements conducing to public mischief
section_353.description: Punishes statements conducing to public mischief, including rumours alarming the public or promoting enmity: up to three years, or fine, or both, rising to five years for enmity-promoting statements.
key_points: Covers fake news and rumour-mongering

section_354.title: Act caused by inducing person to believe that he will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure
section_354.description: Punishes inducing a person to believe he will face divine displeasure if he does not do something, to compel him: up to one year, or fine, or both.

section_355.title: Misconduct in public by a drunken person
section_355.description: Punishes misconduct in public by a drunken person: simple imprisonment up to twenty-four hours, or fine, or both, or community service.
key_points: Community service is an available sentence

section_356.title: Defamation
section_356.description: Defines defamation, making or publishing imputations harming a person's reputation, with ten exceptions including truth for public good and fair comment, and punishes it with up to two years, or fine, or both, or community service.
key_points: Ten statutory exceptions, including truth in public interest
Community service is an available sentence
The former IPC 500 offence

section_357.title: Breach of contract to attend on and supply wants of helpless person
section_357.description: Punishes breach of contract to attend on and supply the wants of a helpless person: up to three months, or fine, or both.

section_358.title: Repeal and savings
section_358.description: Repeals the Indian Penal Code, 1860, while saving actions taken, punishments incurred and proceedings begun under it, which continue under the corresponding provisions of the Sanhita.
key_points: The IPC stands repealed from 1 July 2024
Past convictions and pending cases are preserved
